units.en: Fourth year of Jiaqing (1799), jiwei
units.literal: Fourth year of Jiaqing, jiwei

units.zh: 高宗又以舊記星紀，間有疏漏，御製璣衡撫辰儀，重加測候。
units.en: Qianlong, finding gaps in older star catalogs, built the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and remeasured the sky.
units.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again, because old star records had occasional gaps, personally made the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and took new observations.

units.zh: 乾隆六十年以後，國史無徵，則從闕焉。
units.en: After Qianlong 60 the Veritable Records offer no material, so the account stops there.
units.literal: After Qianlong year 60 the National History has no testimony, and those years are therefore omitted.

units.zh: 今以康熙年間實測各省及諸蒙古高度、偏度，並乾隆時憲所增省分，與回疆部落、兩金川土司等，晝夜永短，節氣早晚，推得高度、偏度備列焉。
units.en: Here Kangxi surveys, Qianlong additions, Xinjiang, and Jinchuan observations yield revised polar altitudes and longitudinal offsets.
units.literal: Now from Kangxi-era actual surveys of each province and Mongol banners, plus provinces added in the Qianlong Time Constitution, together with Muslim borderland tribes and the two Jinchuan chieftaincies — day and night length, solar-term timing — heights and offsets are derived and fully listed.

units.zh: 有清統一區夏，聖聖相承。
units.en: The Qing unified China, one sage emperor following another.
units.literal: The Qing unified All-under-Heaven, sage succeeding sage.

units.zh: 迨平定回疆及兩金川，復令重度裏差，增入時憲。
units.en: After pacifying Xinjiang and the two Jinchuan campaigns, he ordered li-cha remeasured and entered into the Shixian calendar.
units.literal: When the Muslim borderlands and the Two Jinchuan were pacified, he again ordered remeasurement of li-cha and added the results to the Time Constitution calendar.

units.zh: 四十二年，署雲貴總督圖思德奏：「懵駁已死，子贅角牙立，輸誠納貢，原歸中國人。
units.en: In the forty-second year, acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Tuside memorialized: "Meng Bo has died. His son Zhuajiaoya has succeeded him, professed allegiance, offered tribute, and is willing to return Chinese subjects.
units.literal: In the forty-second year, the acting Yunnan-Guizhou governor Tusi De memorialized: "Meng Bo is dead; his son Zhuajiaoya has succeeded, offers loyalty and tribute, and wishes to return to Chinese rule.

units.zh: 請開關通市。」
units.en: He asks that the border be opened for trade."
units.literal: He requests that the border be opened for trade."

units.zh: 尋改直上書房，授三阿哥讀。
units.en: He was soon transferred to the Upper Study to tutor the Third Imperial Son.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Upper Study to instruct the Third Imperial Son.

units.zh: 上諭：「不但授讀講習詩文，當教阿哥為人居心以忠厚為本。」
units.en: The emperor instructed him: "You must teach the prince more than poetry and prose — you must ground his character in sincerity and loyalty."
units.literal: The emperor instructed: "You must not only teach reading and lecture on poetry and prose; you should teach the prince that in conduct of life sincerity and loyalty are the foundation."

units.zh: 系英請加授資治通鑑，以知古今治亂興衰之故，悉民間疾苦，上韙之。
units.en: Xiying asked to add the Comprehensive Mirror so the prince would understand how dynasties rise and fall and know the people's hardships; the emperor approved.
units.literal: Xiying asked to add instruction in the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government so that the prince might know the causes of rise and fall through the ages and understand the people's hardships; the emperor approved.

units.zh: 宋蘇軾自定武謫官過真定，承亮以文謁之，大為稱賞。
units.en: When Su Shi of the Song, demoted from Dingwu, passed through Zhending, Chengliang presented his writings and won high praise.
units.literal: When Su Shi of the Song, demoted from Dingwu, passed through Zhending, Chengliang presented his writings to him and was greatly praised.

units.zh: 壽州武舉張大有因妒姦毒斃族侄張倫及僱工人，總督鐵保徇蘇州知府週鍔以自中蛇毒定讞，彭齡推鞫得實，詔嘉之，特予議敘，鐵保等降黜有差。
units.en: At Shouzhou the military licentiate Zhang Dayou, jealous over an affair, poisoned his clansman Zhang Lun and a hired laborer. Governor-General Tie Bao followed Suzhou Prefect Zhou E in ruling death by self-inflicted snakebite. Pengling re-examined the case and proved murder; the emperor praised him, granted a special merit citation, and Tie Bao and others were demoted in varying degrees.
units.literal: At Shouzhou the military licentiate Zhang Dayou, out of jealous adultery, poisoned his clansman Zhang Lun and a hired worker to death. Governor-General Tie Bao followed Suzhou Prefect Zhou E in ruling death by self-inflicted snake venom. Pengling re-examined the case and established the truth; the emperor praised this, specially granted him a merit citation, and Tie Bao and others were demoted to varying degrees.

units.zh: 十一年，偕侍郎英和往陝西讞獄，途經山西，命察議河東鹽務。
units.en: In the eleventh year, with Vice Minister Ying He, he went to Shaanxi to judge cases; passing Shanxi he was ordered to investigate Hedong salt affairs.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Vice Minister Ying He, he went to Shaanxi to judge cases; passing through Shanxi he was ordered to investigate and deliberate on Hedong salt affairs.

units.zh: 至十八年林清逆黨之變，上思其言，特賜祭焉。
units.en: By 1813, when Lin Qing's rebels struck, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrificial rites in his honor.
units.literal: By the eighteenth year, when Lin Qing's rebel faction rose, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrificial rites.

units.zh: 林清既誅，滑縣逆匪尋平，論功，迭被優敘，賜子淳為郎中。
units.en: After Lin Qing was executed, the Hua County rebels were soon pacified; in accounting merit Gao received repeated preferential commendation, and his son Chun was given a directorship in a ministry.
units.literal: After Lin Qing was executed, the rebels of Hua County were soon pacified; in accounting merit Gao received repeated preferential commendation, and his son Chun was given the post of director in a ministry.

units.zh: 林清逆黨突入禁城，時回鑾，中途聞變，有議俟調大兵成列而後進者，誥曰：「是滋亂也，獻俘者行至矣！」
units.en: Lin Qing's rebels suddenly entered the Forbidden City; the court was returning from Rehe and heard of the disturbance en route; some proposed waiting until large forces were assembled before advancing—Gao said, "That would only encourage disorder; the captors are already on their way!"
units.literal: Lin Qing's rebel faction suddenly entered the Forbidden City; at that time the court was returning from Rehe; midway they heard of the disturbance; some proposed waiting until large forces were assembled in formation before advancing—Gao said, "That would only encourage disorder; those who present captives are already on the road!"

units.zh: 漕運旗丁苦累，屢議加徵調劑，偕漕督鐵保疏陳：「原徵隨漕項下有款可撥，以裨運丁；
units.en: Transport banner soldiers were overburdened and repeated proposals called for extra levies. With Transport Director Tie Bao he wrote: "Funds already collected under transport tax items can be allocated to aid the transport soldiers;
units.literal: Transport banner soldiers suffered hardship; repeated proposals were made to add levies for relief; together with Transport Director Tie Bao he memorialized: "Under the original transport tax items there are funds that can be allocated to aid the transport soldiers;

units.zh: 又旗丁月米，令州縣改給折色，應領運費，責糧道放給，以免層層剝削。」
units.en: banner soldiers' monthly grain rations should be paid in commuted silver by local officials, and transport fees should be issued by the grain intendant to stop layer upon layer of exaction."
units.literal: furthermore, for banner soldiers' monthly grain, let prefectures and counties pay in commuted silver; transport fees due should be issued by the grain intendant, to avoid layer upon layer of exaction."

units.zh: 方督師寧波時，奏請學政劉鳳誥代辦鄉試監臨，有聯號弊，為言官論劾，遣使鞫實，詔斥徇庇，褫職，予編修，在文穎館行走。
units.en: While commanding at Ningbo he asked educational commissioner Liu Fenggao to supervise the provincial exams in his place; linked examination numbers were exposed; censors impeached him; an investigator confirmed it; an edict rebuked his favoritism, stripped his rank, and gave him compiler duty in the Wenyin Hall.
units.literal: While directing troops at Ningbo he memorialized that educational commissioner Liu Fenggao supervise the provincial examination in his stead; linked examination numbers were discovered; censors impeached him; an envoy investigated and confirmed the facts; an edict rebuked him for favoritism, stripped his post, and gave him compiler rank with duty in the Wenyin Hall.

units.zh: 姜晟金光悌祖之望韓崶
units.en: Jiang Cheng, Jin Guangti, Zu Zhiwang, and Han Feng
units.literal: Jiang Cheng, Jin Guangti, Zu Zhiwang, Han Feng

units.zh: 祖之望，字舫齋，福建浦城人。
units.en: Zu Zhiwang, whose courtesy name was Fangzhai, came from Pucheng in Fujian.
units.literal: Zu Zhiwang, courtesy name Fangzhai, was a native of Pucheng in Fujian.

units.zh: 姜晟、祖之望，敭歷中外，並有政績。
units.en: Jiang Cheng and Zu Zhiwang served widely in the capital and provinces and both left solid records of governance.
units.literal: Jiang Cheng and Zu Zhiwang served in posts both within the capital and in the provinces and both had administrative achievements.

units.zh: 乾隆四十三年進士，選庶吉士，散館授刑部主事，洊升郎中。
units.en: He took his jinshi degree in 1778, entered the Hanlin Academy, and on leaving was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, rising step by step to director.
units.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and after leaving the academy was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, then was promoted repeatedly to director.

units.zh: 尋丁母憂，服闋，擢刑部尚書。
units.en: After his mother died and mourning ended, he was promoted to minister of punishments.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 五十八年，出為山西按察使。
units.en: In 1793 he was posted as judicial commissioner of Shanxi.
units.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he went out as Shanxi provincial judicial commissioner.

units.zh: 五年，授湖南巡撫。
units.en: In 1800 he was appointed governor of Hunan.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed governor of Hunan.

units.zh: 七年，命赴山東按皁役之孫冒考，巡撫和瑛誣斷事，和瑛譴罷，即授之望巡撫。
units.en: In 1802 he was sent to Shandong to investigate a runner's grandson who had taken the exams fraudulently. Governor Hewang had misjudged the case, was dismissed, and Zhiwang was appointed governor in his place.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to go to Shandong to investigate a yamen runner's grandson who had fraudulently taken the examination. Governor Hewang had wrongly decided the case; Hewang was rebuked and dismissed, and Zhiwang was immediately appointed governor.

units.zh: 上知之望無染指，居官有聲，素諳刑名，以按察使降補。
units.en: Knowing he had taken nothing for himself, had a strong reputation, and was expert in criminal law, the emperor reappointed him at the lower rank of judicial commissioner.
units.literal: The emperor knew Zhiwang had not dipped his hand into the funds, that in office he had a good reputation, and that he was long versed in criminal law; he was demoted and reappointed as provincial judicial commissioner.

units.zh: 尋復召為刑部侍郎。
units.en: He was soon recalled again as vice minister of punishments.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was again recalled as vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 摘律例民間易犯罪名條列之，曰三尺須知錄，刊布於眾，俾民無誤罹法。
units.en: He compiled the statutes' common offenses into a handbook called Records of What the People Must Know, published it widely, and helped common people avoid unwitting violations of the law.
units.literal: He extracted from the statutes and precedents the offenses commonly committed among the people and listed them in a work called Records of What the People Must Know, published it widely, and thereby kept the people from unwittingly violating the law.

units.zh: 論曰：有清一代，於刑部用人最慎。
units.en: The historian remarks: Throughout the Qing, appointments to the Ministry of Punishments were made with exceptional care.
units.literal: The commentary says: Throughout the Qing dynasty, appointments to the Ministry of Punishments were made with the greatest care.

units.zh: 歷通政司參議、太常寺少卿，仍兼部務。
units.en: He served as counselor in the Office of Transmission and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining concurrent duty in the ministry.
units.literal: He served successively as counselor in the Office of Transmission and as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, while still holding concurrent ministry duties.

units.zh: 六十年，遷雲南布政使。
units.en: In 1795 he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Yunnan.
units.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to be provincial treasurer of Yunnan.

units.zh: 上以之望親老，調湖北，俾便迎養。
units.en: Because his parents were elderly, the emperor moved him to Hubei so he could care for them more easily.
units.literal: Because Zhiwang's parents were elderly, the emperor transferred him to Hubei so that he might more conveniently support them.

units.zh: 二年，丁父憂，命留任素服治事。
units.en: In 1797, when his father died, he was ordered to remain in office and govern in mourning dress.
units.literal: In the second year he entered mourning for his father and was ordered to remain in office and conduct affairs in plain mourning dress.

units.zh: 踰月，授刑部侍郎，予假葬父省母。
units.en: Within a month he was made vice minister of punishments and granted leave to bury his father and visit his mother.
units.literal: After more than a month he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments and granted leave to bury his father and visit his mother.

units.zh: 逾一年，以母老乞養歸。
units.en: A year later, pleading his mother's age, he asked to retire and care for her at home.
units.literal: After more than a year, citing his mother's age, he requested leave to support her and returned home.

units.zh: 總督巡撫皆統師出，之望一人留武昌治事，訛言數作，時獲賊諜，偽檄遍通衢。
units.en: While the governor-general and governors marched out with the armies, Zhiwang alone stayed at Wuchang to run the province. Rumors flared, rebel agents were caught, and forged proclamations appeared on every street.
units.literal: The governor-general and governors all took command of armies and went out; Zhiwang alone remained at Wuchang to manage affairs. Rumors arose repeatedly, rebel spies were captured from time to time, and forged proclamations were posted throughout the streets.

units.zh: 之望靜定不驚，防禦要隘，城鄉市鎮設保甲互稽，民心帖然。
units.en: He kept his composure, fortified the critical passes, and set up mutual surveillance through baojia in town and country until the people were reassured.
units.literal: Zhiwang remained calm and unalarmed, defended the key passes, and established mutual surveillance through baojia in cities, towns, and marketplaces; popular sentiment settled.

units.zh: 賊犯孝感，調師翦滅，下游五郡皆安堵。
units.en: When rebels struck Xiaogan, he moved troops and destroyed them, and the five downstream prefectures were secured.
units.literal: When the rebels attacked Xiaogan, he shifted troops and wiped them out; the five downstream prefectures all returned to peace.

units.zh: 詔以之望雖未與賊戰，坐鎮根本，武、漢無虞，嘉其功，賜花翎。
units.en: The court praised him for holding the rear secure though he had not fought in the field, keeping Wuhan safe, and awarded him the peacock feather.
units.literal: An edict said that although Zhiwang had not fought the rebels in person, by holding the base secure he had kept Wuhan free from alarm; his merit was praised and he was granted the peacock feather.

units.zh: 及讞定，之望坐徇庇降調。
units.en: When the case was decided, Zhiwang was demoted for having shielded him.
units.literal: When the judgment was finalized, Zhiwang was punished for shielding him and was demoted and transferred.

units.zh: 鎮筸黑苗出峒焚掠，蔓延三廳，遣兵擊平之。
units.en: When Black Miao from Zhenqian raided out of the hills and spread through three subprefectures, he sent troops and put the rising down.
units.literal: The Black Miao of Zhenqian came out of their stockades to burn and plunder, spreading through the three subprefectures; he sent troops and suppressed them.

units.zh: 至京，面陳永綏廳孤懸苗境，不足資控制，請移廳治花園，移協營茶洞，沿邊遍設碉卡，以永綏舊城為汛地，使苗弁駐闉，約束諸苗寨，下所司議行。
units.en: In Beijing he argued in audience that Yongsui Subprefecture, isolated in the Miao country, could not hold the frontier. He proposed moving the seat to Huayuan, shifting the garrison to Chadong, building blockhouses along the border, turning the old Yongsui town into a garrison post, and posting Miao officers there to control the stockades. The court referred his plan to the responsible offices for action.
units.literal: On reaching the capital he stated in audience that Yongsui Subprefecture stood isolated in the Miao country and was inadequate for control; he requested moving the subprefectural seat to Huayuan, moving the garrison brigade to Chadong, setting watchtowers and checkpoints all along the border, using the old Yongsui city as a garrison post, and stationing Miao officers in the walled town to restrain the Miao stockades. The matter was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.

units.zh: 六年，偕侍郎那彥寶勘近畿水災，又偕侍郎高杞監疏長辛店河道。
units.en: In 1801 he joined Vice Minister Nayinbao to inspect flood damage near the capital, and Vice Minister Gao Qi to supervise dredging at Changxindian.
units.literal: In the sixth year, together with Vice Minister Nayinbao, he surveyed flood damage in the capital region; together with Vice Minister Gao Qi he supervised dredging of the Changxindian river channel.

units.zh: 尋調陝西。
units.en: He was soon transferred to Shaanxi.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Shaanxi.

units.zh: 調廣東，乞假省親。
units.en: Transferred to Guangdong, he asked for leave to visit his family.
units.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong and requested leave to visit his family.

units.zh: 九年，仍授刑部侍郎。
units.en: In 1804 he was again made vice minister of punishments.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was again appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 十四年，仁宗五旬萬壽，之望入都祝嘏。
units.en: In 1809, for Jiaqing's fiftieth-birthday celebration, he came to Beijing to offer congratulations.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the Renzong Emperor's fiftieth-birthday celebration, Zhiwang entered the capital to offer congratulations.

units.zh: 十八年，以病解職，尋卒。
units.en: In 1813 he resigned because of illness and soon died.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year he left office because of illness and soon died.

units.zh: 嘉慶元年，教匪起荊、襄，蔓延鄖、宜、施南諸郡。
units.en: In 1796 White Lotus rebels broke out in Jing and Xiang and spread through Yun, Yi, and the Shinan region.
units.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing sectarian rebels rose in Jing and Xiang, spreading through the prefectures of Yun, Yi, and Shinan.

units.zh: 四年，安襄鄖道胡齊崙侵餉事發，命之望察治，齊崙侵蝕餽送，轇轕猝不易究，上切責之，命解任來京。
units.en: In 1799 the embezzlement of army pay by Circuit Intendant Hu Qilun of An-Xiang-Yun came to light. Zhiwang was ordered to investigate, but Qilun's diversions of supplies and transport funds proved too tangled to sort out quickly. The emperor rebuked him sharply and ordered him relieved and summoned to Beijing.
units.literal: In the fourth year the case of An-Xiang-Yun circuit intendant Hu Qilun's embezzlement of military pay came to light. Zhiwang was ordered to investigate. Qilun had embezzled supplies and transport funds; the tangle of accounts was suddenly hard to unravel. The emperor sharply rebuked him and ordered him relieved of office and summoned to the capital.

units.zh: 契丹地直京師東北五千里而贏，東距高麗，西奚，南營州，北靺鞨、室韋，阻冷陘山以自固。射獵居處無常。其君大賀氏有勝兵四萬，析八部，臣于突厥，以為俟斤。凡調發攻戰，則諸部畢會，獵則部得自行。與奚不平，每鬬不利，輒遁保鮮卑山。武德初，武德初 初原作「中」，據下文二年及舊唐書一九九下契丹傳改。大帥孫敖曹與靺鞨長突地稽俱來朝。二年，入犯平州境。六年，君長咄羅獻名馬、豐貂。貞觀二年，摩會來降，突厥請以梁師都易契丹，太宗曰：「契丹、突厥不同類，師都唐編戶，我將擒之，不可易降者。」三年，摩會入朝，賜鼓纛，由是有常貢。帝伐高麗，悉發契丹、奚首領從軍。還過營州，以窟哥為左武衞將軍。大帥辱紇主據曲率眾來歸，辱紇主據曲 辱紇主原誤「紇主」，據新唐書二一九契丹傳改。據曲，參卷三二校勘記[七]。即其部為玄州，以據曲為刺史，隸營州都督府。窟哥舉部內屬，乃置松漠都督府，以窟哥為都督，封無極男，賜姓李氏。以達稽部為峭落州，紇便部為彈汗州，獨活部為無逢州，芬問部羽陵州，突便部為日連州，芮奚部為徒河州，墜斤部為萬丹州，伏部為匹黎、赤山二州，俱隸松漠府，以辱紇主為刺史。窟哥死，與奚叛，行軍總管阿史德樞賓執松漠都督阿不固，阿不固 按新唐書契丹傳作阿卜固。獻于東都。窟哥二孫：曰枯莫離，彈汗州刺史、歸順郡王；曰盡忠，松漠都督。敖曹曾孫曰萬榮，敖曹曾孫曰萬榮 曾孫，舊唐書契丹傳同。新唐書契丹傳作「有孫曰萬榮」。歸誠州刺史。時營州都督趙文翽數侵侮其下，盡忠等怨望，與萬榮共舉兵，殺文翽，據營州，自號「無上可汗」，推萬榮為帥。不二旬，眾數萬，攻崇州，執擊討副使許欽寂。武后怒，詔將軍曹仁師等二十八將擊之，更號萬榮曰「萬斬」，盡忠曰「盡滅」。戰西硤石黃獐谷，王師敗績。進攻平州，不克。武后益發兵擊契丹。萬榮夜襲檀州，清邊道副總管張九節拒戰，萬榮敗走。俄盡忠死，突厥默啜襲破其部。萬榮收散兵，復振。別將駱務整、何阿小入冀州，殺刺史陸寶積，掠數千人。武后聞盡忠死，詔夏官尚書王孝傑等率兵十七萬討萬榮，戰東硤石，敗績，孝傑死之，萬榮進屠幽州。又詔御史大夫婁師德等率兵二十萬擊之，萬榮乘銳，鼓行而南，殘瀛州屬縣。神兵道總管楊玄基率奚掩擊，神兵道總管楊玄基 原作神兵總管楊立基，據新唐書契丹傳改。大破萬榮，執何阿小，別將李楷固、駱務整降。萬榮委軍走，玄基與奚四面合擊，萬榮眾潰，東走。張九節設三伏待之。萬榮窮蹙，與家奴輕騎走潞河東，憊甚，臥林下。奴斬其首以獻，九節傳東都。契丹餘眾不能立，遂附突厥。開元二年，盡忠從父弟失活率部落歸唐。 : 失活，玄宗賜丹書鐵券。開元四年，與奚長李大酺偕來，詔復置松漠府，以失活為都督，封松漠郡王；仍置靜析軍；以失活為經略大使，八部長皆為刺史。五年，以楊氏為永樂公主下嫁失活。五年以楊氏為永樂公主下嫁失活 按舊唐書契丹傳，「開元三年，其首領李失活率種落內附。明年，失活入朝，封宗室外甥女楊氏為永樂公主以妻之。」六年，卒。 : 娑固，失活之弟，帝以娑固襲爵。開元七年十一月，娑固與公主來朝。衙官可突于勇悍，得眾心，娑固欲除之；事泄，可突于攻之，娑固奔營州。都督許欽澹及奚君李大酺攻可突于，不勝，娑固、大酺皆死。（韓愈作可突干，劉昫、宋祁及唐會要皆作可突于。） : 鬱于，娑固從父弟也，可突于推以為主，遣使謝罪，玄宗冊立襲娑固位。開元十年，鬱于入朝，以慕容氏為燕郡公主下嫁鬱于，卒。 : 咄于，咄于 units.en: Khitan territory lay five thousand li northeast of the capital, stretching east to Goguryeo, west to the Xi, south to Yingzhou, and north to the Mohe and Shiwei, with the Lengling range as their barrier. They hunted for a living and moved their camps at will. The Dahe chiefs commanded forty thousand warriors organized in eight tribes; they acknowledged the Turks as overlords and served as irkin. All tribes mustered for war, but each could hunt on its own. They feuded constantly with the Xi, usually lost, and retreated to the Xianbei Mountains. Early in the Wude era — the opening "chu" was originally written "zhong," corrected from the year-2 notice and Jiu Tang Shu 199b — Grand Chief Sun Aocao and the Mohe leader Tudi Ji presented themselves at court. In year 2 they raided Pingzhou. In year 6 Chief Zhuoluo offered fine horses and pelts. In Zhenguan year 2 Mo Hui surrendered; when the Turks asked to swap Liang Shidu for the Khitan, Taizong replied, "Khitan and Turk are not kin; Shidu is a subject household of Tang — I mean to take him — and I will not trade away those who have submitted." Mo Hui visited court in year 3, received drums and banners, and thereafter paid regular tribute. Campaigning against Goguryeo, the emperor drafted every Khitan and Xi leader. On the return through Yingzhou he appointed Kuge Left Martial Guard General. The grand chieftain Quju brought his people in; ruhezhu was his chiefly title, while the parallel account reverses the transmitted name Juqu to Quju. See Xin Tang Shu 219 and juan 32 note [7]. His band became Xuan Prefecture under Juqu, attached to Yingzhou. When Kuge led the whole tribe inward, Songmo Protectorate was founded: Kuge became protector, was enfeoffed Lord of Wuji, and received the surname Li. The Daqi became Qiaoluo Prefecture, Hebian Tanhan, Duhuo Wufeng, Fenwen Yuling, Tubian Rilian, Ruixi Tuhe, Zhuijin Wandan, and the Fu line the twin prefectures Pili and Chishan — all under Songmo, with their respective chieftains as prefects. After Kuge's death they rebelled with the Xi; campaigning general Ashide Shubin seized Songmo protector Abu Gu (A Bu Gu in Xin Tang Shu) and sent him to Luoyang. Kuge left two grandsons: Kumoli, Tanhan prefect and Prince of Guishun, and Jinzhong, Songmo protector. Aocao's great-grandson Wanrong — the line repeats; Jiu Tang Shu agrees; Xin Tang Shu reads "had a grandson Wanrong" — held Guicheng Prefecture. Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenbi bullied their people until Jinzhong and Wanrong rose together, killed Wenbi, seized Yingzhou, proclaimed themselves "Supreme Khans," and made Wanrong commander. Within twenty days they mustered tens of thousands, took Chongzhou, and captured suppression vice-commissioner Xu Qinji. Empress Wu sent Generals Cao Renshi and twenty-seven others, renaming Wanrong "Wan the Beheaded" and Jinzhong "Jin the Exterminated." At Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi the imperial force was routed. They failed to capture Pingzhou. Wu sent more troops. Wanrong struck Tanzhou by night; Zhang Jiujie of the Qingbian command drove him off. Jinzhong soon died and Turk Mokchuo shattered the tribe. Wanrong regrouped. Lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao entered Jizhou, killed prefect Lu Baoji, and carried off thousands. Learning of Jinzhong's death, Wu ordered Wang Xiaojie and one hundred seventy thousand men against Wanrong; at East Xiashi they were beaten, Xiaojie was killed, and Wanrong sacked Youzhou. Lou Shide followed with two hundred thousand; Wanrong marched south in full vigor and ravaged Yingzhou's counties. Shenbing commander Yang Xuanji — the text's Yang Liji is wrong per Xin Tang Shu — led Xi auxiliaries, crushed Wanrong, captured He Axiao, and accepted the surrender of Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng. Wanrong abandoned his army; Xuanji and the Xi closed in from four sides until his host broke and fled east. Zhang Jiujie laid three ambushes. Cornered, Wanrong fled east of the Lu River with a household slave; exhausted, he lay under trees while the slave took his head to Jiujie, who sent it to Luoyang. The Khitan remnant could not endure and joined the Turks. In Kaiyuan year 2 Jinzhong's cousin Shihuo brought the tribe back. : Shihuo received an iron certificate from Xuanzong. In Kaiyuan year 4 he came with Xi chief Li Dachi; the court restored Songmo, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, re-created the Jingxi Army, appointed him frontier commissioner, and made the eight chiefs prefects. In year 5 the Yang clanswoman became Princess Yongle and married him — per Jiu Tang Shu, "In Kaiyuan year 3 their chief Li Shihuo led his tribes to submit inward; the next year Shihuo entered court, and the emperor's clanswoman Yang was made Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage." He died in year 6. : Suogu, Shihuo's brother, inherited. In Kaiyuan 7/11 Suogu and the princess attended court. Yamen officer Ketuyu was bold and popular; Suogu tried to kill him, the plot failed, Ketuyu attacked, and Suogu fled to Yingzhou. Protector Xu Qindan and Xi lord Li Dachi attacked Ketuyu, failed, and both died. (Han Yu writes Ketugan; Liu Xu, Song Qi, and Tang Huiyao write Ketuyu.) : Yuyu, Suogu's cousin, was set up by Ketuyu, apologized to court, and Xuanzong confirmed him in Suogu's place. In Kaiyuan 10 Yuyu came to court; a Murong clanswoman became Princess of Yancheng and married him; he died. : Tuyu (Zhuoyu in this text; Tuyu in both Tang histories and Tongkao 345), Yuyu's brother, succeeded. In Kaiyuan 13 he quarreled with Ketuyu and fled with the princess; the court enfeoffed him Prince of Liaoyang (Commandery in both Tang histories). : Shaogu, Tuyu's brother — both Tang histories say Li Jinzhong's brother — was raised by the people. In Kaiyuan 13 winter he attended the mobile court, joined the Fengshan at Mount Tai, became Prince of Guanghua, and a Chen clanswoman became Princess Dongguang (Donghua in both Tang histories) and married him. In year 18 Ketuyu murdered him, led the people to the Turks, and the princess fled to Pinglu. : Qulie (Qulie in Xin Tang Shu; Zhang Jiuling's Qujiang ji 8 has Julei), lineage unknown, enthroned by Ketuyu. In Kaiyuan 22/6 Zhang Shougui of Youzhou — both histories say chief administrator; his title was "Vice Military Commissioner of Youzhou, Chief Administrator of Youzhou, and Censor-in-Chief," per Qujiang ji 9 — routed Ketuyu. In month 12 he won again, beheaded Qulie, Ketuyu, and others, sent heads to Luoyang; survivors hid in the hills. Guo-zhe (Yujie in Qujiang ji 5 and 8; guo may stand for yu) was a Khitan chief and Songmo yamen officer who killed Ketuyu and Qulie and submitted. Zhang Shougui made him Prince of Beiping. That year Ketuyu's follower Ni-li killed Guo-zhe and exterminated his house; son Lagan escaped to Andong as Left Xiaowei General. Thereafter the Khitan waned; the Dahe clung to the Xi king to reach Tang with yearly tribute: twice in Zhide–Baoying, thirteen visits in the Dali era (not "the twelfth year of Dali"; the era lasted fourteen years), thrice in Zhenyuan 9–11, seven in Yuanhe, four in Taihe and Kaicheng. Ni-li — Nieli in Yelü Yan, Yali in Chen Daren — was ancestor to Liao Taizu. Li Huaixiu, given Tang name and surname, Khitan name Dilian Zuli (Zuli above), was chief of the eight tribes. In Tianbao 4 he surrendered and became Songmo protector. An Lushan asked to campaign against the Khitan; the text says Huaixiu raised one hundred thousand — Xin Tang Shu says Lushan raised over one hundred thousand from four commands, not Huaixiu's army — and defeated Lushan south of the Huangshui, after which war with Lushan never ceased. Yelü Yan records that Taizu's fourth-generation forebear Noulishi, yilijin of the Yila, sent Zhiligu and Kulie to rout Fan Yang Lushan at the Huangshui in Huaixiu's day; Huaixiu was thus the first Yaolian lord and Zuwu Khan. Kai-luo, enfeoffed Prince Gongren, replaced the Songmo protector and was called Khitan king. The state grew; in Zhenyuan 4 it raided the north and Youzhou reported. After Lushan's rebellion Hebei warlords blocked the roads and many generations are lost — yet Officials Treatise 1 lists nine Yaolian khans in the Nine Accounts office. : King Qushu, in Huichang 2 made Cloud-Banner General, was Yelan Khan — the title was misplaced under a Youzhou commissioner entry and is corrected per Xin Tang Shu. Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu said the Khitan still used Uyghur seals and begged a new imperial seal inscribed "Khitan Serving the State" (Goryeo's record has Quxu). : King Xier (Xierzhi in Xin Tang Shu) was Bala Khan; in Xiantong he twice sent tribute and the tribes strengthened. : King Qinde of Xier's line was Hendejin Khan; in Guangqi he raided Xi and Shiwei until all served him and fought Liu Rengong repeatedly; late in life his rule failed. Great men of the eight tribes rotated every three years, but Yila chief Yelü Abaoji raised his own banners, refused rotation, called himself king, seized all Khitan lands, and ended the Yaolian. : Xiao Hanjianu held that after Yaolian Khan Wa the line broke until yilijin Yali enthroned the Zuwu Khan. Comparing Tang and Liao sources, the Dahe ended with Shaogu; Yali's enthronement was Huaixiu; only Qulie and Guo-zhe lay between. Qulie was Ketuyu's puppet; Guo-zhe, a collateral chief, was killed by Yali. Tang history calls Ni-li Ketuyu's remnant — so was Wa perhaps Qulie?
units.literal: The Khitan lands lay five thousand li northeast of the capital and were expansive; east they bordered Goguryeo, west the Xi, south Yingzhou, north Mohe and Shiwei, securing themselves behind the Lengling Mountains. They hunted and had no fixed dwellings. Their ruler of the Dahe clan had forty thousand effective troops, divided into eight tribes, and submitted to the Turks as irkin. Whenever mobilized for attack or war all tribes assembled; for hunting each tribe could act on its own. They were at odds with the Xi; whenever they fought they fared poorly and fled to shelter on the Xianbei Mountains. At the beginning of Wude — chu was originally zhong, corrected per the account below for year 2 and Jiu Tang Shu 199b Khitan Account — Grand Chieftain Sun Aocao and the Mohe chief Tudi Ji both came to court. In year 2 they invaded Pingzhou territory. In year 6 Chieftain Zhuoluo presented famous horses and rich sables. In Zhenguan year 2 Mo Hui came to surrender; the Turks asked to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan, and Taizong said: "The Khitan and Turks are not the same kind; Shidu is a Tang registered household — I will capture him — one cannot exchange a surrendered people." In year 3 Mo Hui entered court and was given drums and banners; thereafter there was regular tribute. When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo he mobilized all Khitan and Xi leaders to follow the army. Returning through Yingzhou he made Kuge Left Martial Guard General. The ruhezhu Quju, a grand chieftain, led his people to submit — the transmitted name Juqu is reversed to Quju in the parallel account, while ruhezhu is the Khitan chiefly title; see Xin Tang Shu 219 and juan 32 collation [7]. His tribe was made Xuanzhou with Juqu as prefect, subordinate to Yingzhou Protectorate. Kuge brought his whole tribe to submit inward; Songmo Protectorate was then established with Kuge as protector, enfeoffed as Lord of Wuji, surname Li bestowed. The Daqi tribe became Qiaoluo Prefecture, the Hebian tribe Tanhan Prefecture, the Duhuo tribe Wufeng Prefecture, the Fenwen tribe Yuling Prefecture, the Tubian tribe Rilian Prefecture, the Ruixi tribe Tuhe Prefecture, the Zhuijin tribe Wandan Prefecture, the Fu tribe the two prefectures Pili and Chishan — all subordinate to Songmo, with their respective chieftains as prefects. When Kuge died they rebelled with the Xi; campaigning general Ashide Shubin seized Songmo Protector Abu Gu — Xin Tang Shu reads A Bu Gu — and presented him in the eastern capital. Kuge's two grandsons: Kumoli, Tanhan prefect and Prince of Guishun; Jinzhong, Songmo protector. Aocao's great-grandson was Wanrong — duplicated; Jiu Tang Shu agrees; Xin Tang Shu reads "had a grandson Wanrong" — Guicheng prefect. The Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenbi repeatedly insulted their subordinates; Jinzhong and others resented it and with Wanrong jointly raised troops, killed Wenbi, seized Yingzhou, styled themselves "Supreme Khans," and made Wanrong commander. Within twenty days their force numbered tens of thousands; they attacked Chongzhou and captured Vice Commissioner for Suppression Xu Qinji. Empress Wu was enraged and ordered Generals Cao Renshi and twenty-seven others to attack them, renaming Wanrong "Wan the Beheaded" and Jinzhong "Jin the Exterminated." At Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi the imperial army was defeated. Advancing on Pingzhou they could not take it. Empress Wu sent more troops against the Khitan. Wanrong raided Tanzhou by night; Qingbian Circuit Vice Commander Zhang Jiujie resisted and Wanrong fled. Soon Jinzhong died and the Turk Mokchuo struck and broke their tribe. Wanrong gathered scattered troops and revived. Lieutenant-generals Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao entered Jizhou, killed Prefect Lu Baoji, and plundered several thousand people. Hearing Jinzhong had died, Empress Wu ordered Minister of Summer Works Wang Xiaojie and others with one hundred seventy thousand troops against Wanrong; at East Xiashi they were defeated, Xiaojie died, and Wanrong advanced to slaughter Youzhou. She also ordered Censor-in-Chief Lou Shide and others with two hundred thousand troops; Wanrong with sharp momentum marched south in drum-order and ravaged counties subordinate to Yingzhou. Shenbing Circuit Commander Yang Xuanji led Xi in a flanking strike — originally Shenbing Commander Yang Liji, corrected per Xin Tang Shu — greatly defeated Wanrong, captured He Axiao, and lieutenants Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng surrendered. Wanrong abandoned his army and fled; Xuanji and the Xi struck from four sides, Wanrong's host collapsed and fled east. Zhang Jiujie set three ambushes. Wanrong in extremity fled east of the Lu River with a household slave on light horses, utterly exhausted, lying under a grove; the slave cut off his head and presented it, and Jiujie sent it to the eastern capital. The Khitan remnant could not stand and attached to the Turks. In Kaiyuan year 2 Jinzhong's younger cousin Shihuo led the tribe back to Tang. : Shihuo — Xuanzong bestowed an iron certificate. Kaiyuan year 4 he came with Xi chief Li Dachi; an edict restored Songmo Prefecture, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, re-established the Jingxi Army, made Shihuo frontier commissioner, and the eight tribal chiefs all became prefects. Year 5 the Yang clanswoman was made Princess Yongle and married to Shihuo — per Jiu Tang Shu, year 3 Shihuo submitted, year 4 he attended court and the emperor's clanswoman Yang was made princess. Year 6 he died. : Suogu, Shihuo's younger brother — the emperor had Suogu inherit the title. Kaiyuan year 7 month 11 Suogu and the princess came to court. Yamen officer Ketuyu was fierce and won the people's hearts; Suogu wished to remove him; the plot leaked and Ketuyu attacked; Suogu fled to Yingzhou. Protector Xu Qindan and Xi lord Li Dachi attacked Ketuyu without success; Suogu and Dachi both died. (Han Yu writes Ketugan; Liu Xu, Song Qi, and Tang Huiyao all write Ketuyu.) : Yuyu, Suogu's younger cousin — Ketuyu pushed him as leader, sent envoys to apologize, and Xuanzong enfeoffed him to succeed Suogu. Kaiyuan year 10 Yuyu entered court; the Murong clanswoman was made Princess of Yancheng and married to Yuyu; he died. : Tuyu — written Zhuoyu in this text but Tuyu in both Tang histories and Tongkao 345 — Yuyu's younger brother, inherited office and title. Kaiyuan year 13 Tuyu again clashed with Ketuyu and fled to court with the princess, enfeoffed Prince of Liaoyang — both Tang histories read Prince of Liaoyang Commandery. : Shaogu, Tuyu's younger brother — both Tang histories read younger brother of Li Jinzhong — the people jointly enthroned him. Kaiyuan year 13 winter he attended the traveling palace, followed the Fengshan at Mount Tai, was changed to Prince of Guanghua, and the Chen clanswoman was made Princess Dongguang and married to Shaogu — both Tang histories read Donghua Princess. Year 18 he was assassinated by Ketuyu, who led his people to surrender to the Turks; Princess Dongguang fled to Pinglu. : Qulie — Xin Tang Shu reads Qulie; Zhang Jiuling's Qujiang ji 8 reads Julei — lineage unknown; Ketuyu enthroned him. Kaiyuan year 22 month 6 Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui greatly defeated Ketuyu — both Tang histories read Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhang Shougui; his title then was "Vice Military Commissioner of Youzhou, Chief Administrator and Censor-in-Chief," per Qujiang ji 9. Month 12 he defeated them again, beheaded Qulie and Ketuyu and others, sent heads to the eastern capital; the remainder scattered into the valleys. Guo-zhe — Qujiang ji 5 and 8 read Yujie, 9 and 11 read Guo-zhe; yu and yu sound alike; guo should perhaps be yu — was originally a Khitan tribal chief, Songmo yamen officer, who beheaded Ketuyu and Qulie and submitted to Tang. Zhang Shougui enthroned him and enfeoffed him Prince of Beiping. That year Ketuyu's remnant Ni-li assassinated Guo-zhe and slaughtered his family; one son Lagan fled to Andong and was appointed Left Xiaowei General. From this the Khitan declined; the Dahe attached themselves as vassals to the Xi king to reach Tang, tribute coming yearly. Between Zhide and Baoying they came twice; in Dali thirteen times — originally miswritten Dali year 12, corrected per Xin Tang Shu; Dali had fourteen years, roughly once a year — Zhenyuan years 9–11 three times, Yuanhe seven times, Taihe and Kaicheng four times. Ni-li — Yelü Yan's Liao history writes Nieli, Chen Daren writes Yali — was the progenitor of Liao Taizu. Li Huaixiu, Tang bestowed name and surname, Khitan name Dilian Zuli — above written Zuli — originally great chief of the eight tribes. Tianbao year 4 he surrendered to Tang and was appointed Songmo protector. An Lushan memorialized to campaign against the Khitan; Huaixiu raised one hundred thousand troops — per Xin Tang Shu An Lushan raised more than one hundred thousand from Youzhou, Yunzhong, Pinglu, and Hedong; not Huaixiu's one hundred thousand — fought Lushan south of the Huangshui; Lushan was greatly defeated, and thereafter fighting with Lushan was unceasing. Yelü Yan's annals say Taizu's fourth-generation ancestor Noulishi as Yila tribe yilijin sent generals Zhiligu and Kulie to greatly defeat Fan Yang An Lushan at the Huangshui, exactly in Huaixiu's time; thus Huaixiu was clearly the first lord of the Yaolian and the Zuwu Khan. Kai-luo, enfeoffed by Tang as Prince Gongren, replaced the Songmo protector and was then called Khitan king. Thereafter they gradually grew; Zhenyuan year 4 they raided the northern frontier and Youzhou reported it. From Lushan's rebellion the Hebei was carved up and communications cut; generations cannot all be traced — per Officials Treatise 1 the Yaolian Nine Accounts Grand Constant already lists nine generations of khans. : Khitan King Qushu — in Wuzong's Huichang year 2 appointed Cloud-Banner General — this is Yelan Khan. The phrase "is Yelan Khan" was originally placed under "Youzhou Military Commissioner," mistaking Qushu for commissioner; corrected per Xin Tang Shu. Youzhou Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu memorialized that the Khitan formerly used Uyghur seals and begged a newly made imperial seal; an edict used the text "Khitan Serving the State." (Goryeo's ancient record writes Quxu.) : Khitan King Xier — Xin Tang Shu reads Xierzhi — was Bala Khan. In Xiantong he twice sent envoys with tribute and the tribes grew stronger. : Khitan King Qinde, of Xier's clan, was Hendejin Khan. In Guangqi he raided the Xi and Shiwei tribes and made them all serve; he repeatedly fought Liu Rengong. In his later years government declined. The eight tribal great men were by law replaced every three years; Yila tribe Yelü Abaoji raised banners and drums, made himself a separate tribe, refused rotation, styled himself king, possessed the whole Khitan state, and the Yaolian perished. : Xiao Hanjianu said that after the Yaolian Khan Wa the royal line was cut off, and from yilijin Yali enthroning the Zuwu Khan the great throne was first fixed. Comparing Tang and Liao histories now, the Dahe ended with Shaogu; Yali enthroned Huaixiu; between them were only Qulie and Guo-zhe. Qulie was enthroned by Ketuyu; Guo-zhe as collateral chief was killed by Yali. Tang history calls Ni-li Ketuyu's remnant; then Khan Wa was perhaps Qulie?
